title: Omni-JEV: Text and Dual-Stream Speech Decisions
abstract: arXiv:2611.13777v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: A user utterance does not uniquely determine the next action in full-duplex dialogue: its consequences depend on the assistant's response state and interaction history. Speech activity, utterance completion, and interruption intent provide related evidence, whose implications for a response require an explicit action policy. We formulate this task at collected-segment endpoints and introduce Omni-JEV, which maps text or role-indexed user and assistant-reference speech to probabilities over five interaction actions. An aligned speech-to-speech understanding backbone encodes the acoustic roles separately and shares its candidate readout with text inputs. Bilingual weak supervision supports cross-entropy fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning for probability-sensitive decisions (RLCD). tldr: 提出 Omni-JEV 模型，在全双工对话中将文本或角色索引的双流（用户与助手参考）语音映射为五种交互动作的概率，并通过双语弱监督微调与 RLCD 强化学习实现概率敏感的决策。
en_tdlr: Omni-JEV maps text or role-indexed dual-stream user and assistant-reference speech to probabilities over five interaction actions in full-duplex dialogue, trained via bilingual weak supervision and RLCD reinforcement learning for probability-sensitive decisions.
